Site administrators and users belonging to the event's own organisation retain full visibility, and sync users continue to match soft-deleted elements as intended.

The issue was reported by ENISA.
title: MISP Event Search Discloses Hidden Attribute and Object Data via Missing Sub-Entity Authorization

desc: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the correlations/eventCorrelations endpoint and the underlying correlation engines (Default and OnDemand). The CorrelationsController::eventCorrelations action did not verify that the requesting user was permitted to view the event specified by the event ID parameter. Any authenticated user could supply the ID of an event belonging to another organisation (distribution level 0, organisation-only) and receive its full correlation results, including attribute identifiers and values. Additionally, for events the user could partially view, the correlation engines filtered only the related (target) side of each correlation row and did not vet the queried event's own source attributes. As a result, correlations keyed by attributes hidden from the user (organisation-only attributes, attributes in sharing groups the user is not a member of, or attributes inside organisation-only objects) were returned with their IDs and values. The Default engine's related-event listing (used in events/view) also included events related solely through such hidden attributes. The vulnerability was reported by ENISA. Successful exploitation requires a valid authenticated session with any role and knowledge or enumeration of a target event ID. The security impact is disclosure of threat-intelligence attribute values (IP addresses, domain names, etc.) and attribute identifiers that the user is not authorised to see, as well as confirmation of the existence of otherwise invisible events.
title: MISP Event Correlations Endpoint Missing Authorization on Queried Event and Hidden Attributes

desc: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the user login-email change logic. When an external authentication backend is configured (LDAP, Shibboleth, ApacheSecureAuth, or CustomAuth), the login email address serves as the key by which the directory service resolves a user's identity, organization, and role on each login. The __canChangeLogin() method in UsersController only checked the MISP.disable_user_login_change setting and site-admin status; it did not account for whether an external authentication backend was active. As a result, any authenticated non-admin user (including org admins) could change their own login email to an address that matches a higher-privilege account in the external directory. On the user's next login, the external backend would resolve that email to the target directory identity, granting the attacker the organization and role associated with that identity. This constitutes an account-identity capture and privilege escalation: the attacker effectively assumes the identity of any directory account whose email they can guess or discover. The vulnerability requires an authenticated session with a valid API key or session token and a MISP instance configured with at least one external authentication backend. The impact is limited to the scope of the captured directory identity's privileges within MISP.
title: MISP: Non-admin users can change login email under external authentication to capture a directory identity

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file mainfunction.cgi of the component Apmcfg Upload. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 addresses this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."
title: DrayTek Vigor2960 Apmcfg Upload mainfunction.cgi null pointer dereference

desc: A vulnerability was identified in Relaticle up to 3.10.0. This affects the function mapToField of the file packages/ImportWizard/src/Livewire/Steps/MappingStep.php of the component Import Wizard. Such manipulation of the argument Target leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
title: Relaticle Import Wizard MappingStep.php mapToField authorization

desc: A weakness has been identified in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected is the function setSWMProfile of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi. Executing a manipulation of the argument filename can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."
title: DrayTek Vigor2960 mainfunction.cgi setSWMProfile stack-based overflow

desc: When two templated upstreams in temporal-proxy render the same address, a request routed to one upstream can be sent under the other upstream's credential, namespace translation, and payload encryption keys. temporal-proxy pools connections for templated upstreams by rendered address and TLS server name only, although each upstream's outbound credential, namespace translation, and payload encryption keys, where configured, are attached to its connection. A request routed to one upstream can therefore be sent over the connection the other created, and the upstream Temporal service authorizes it as the other upstream's principal. Configuration validation rejects only identical hostPort values, so templates that differ in text but render the same address are accepted. This mixes the two upstreams' ordinary traffic, and a caller that an external authenticator restricts to one upstream's namespaces can use it to act under the other upstream's credential. Deployments with at most one templated upstream are not affected. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0 through 1.1.1 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.0, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.
title: temporal-proxy can send a request under another upstream's credential when templated upstreams render the same address

desc: A caller with write permission in a namespace can terminate temporal-proxy through memory exhaustion by storing highly compressed payloads in Workflow history, and the stored history causes the same failure on every later read. temporal-proxy 1.2.0 decompresses every payload marked as compressed in the responses it forwards, whether or not compression is configured. Each payload is limited to 4 MiB after decompression, but the total for a response is not, and the decoded payloads are held in memory together. The caller can store many small, highly compressed payloads through the proxy or directly at the upstream Temporal service. When that history is read through the proxy, for example by a Worker processing a task, the proxy can run out of memory and be terminated. The codec server's /decode endpoint is affected in the same way when it is enabled. Only temporal-proxy 1.2.0 is affected; earlier versions do not decompress payloads. The issue is fixed in 1.2.1. Upgrade to 1.2.1 or later.
title: temporal-proxy can be terminated by memory exhaustion when decompressing stored payloads

desc: A caller who can reach the temporal-proxy gRPC listener, with or without a valid credential, can grow the proxy's memory until the process is terminated by sending requests with many distinct gRPC method names. temporal-proxy labels its request metrics with the method name exactly as the caller sent it, and records every request, including those that authentication or routing reject. Each distinct method name adds metric series that are never removed. The series grow whether or not the metrics endpoint is scraped, and metric labels configured from request metadata multiply the growth. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0-alpha.20260716 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.
title: Unauthenticated callers can exhaust temporal-proxy memory through unbounded request metrics

desc: A caller who can send requests to the temporal-proxy gRPC listener can obtain the static API key of an upstream whose address is templated from the request namespace, and then use that key directly against the upstream Temporal service. temporal-proxy does not validate the request namespace before rendering it into a templated upstream address, so when an upstream's hostPort is templated from the namespace, as in the published Temporal Cloud configuration example, a crafted namespace changes the host the proxy dials. If that upstream verifies TLS against the system trust store and sets no literal server name, a caller-controlled host with a publicly trusted certificate passes verification and receives the key. The built-in static-token and JWKS authenticators do not restrict namespaces, so any caller they admit can do this; an external authenticator that admits only listed namespaces prevents it. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line, and rotate any upstream API key that untrusted callers could reach.
title: temporal-proxy request namespace can redirect a templated upstream and leak its API key

desc: SGLang through 0.5.23, fixed in commit 7b5fb39, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /load_lora_adapter_from_tensors HTTP endpoint, which lacks the @auth_level(AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL) decorator applied to its sibling admin endpoints, allowing unauthenticated network-reachable attackers to invoke it without an API key. Attackers can load a LoRA adapter from attacker-supplied serialized tensors to manipulate the served model, and when combined with a separately documented deserialization bypass, achieve unauthenticated remote code execution as root.
title: SGLang 0.5.23 Missing Authorization via load_lora_adapter_from_tensors

desc: temporary redacted
products: meta platforms, inc.:whatsapp messenger for ios
title: Improper Protection of WhatsApp Noise Authentication Key on iOS

desc: IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to a server-side request forgery.
title: IBM Engineering AI hub Server-Side Request Forgery

desc: Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames vulnerability. A high privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of Service and Launch of Phishing Attacks.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme vulnerability. A high privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Client-Side Request Forgery and Information Disclosure.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Incorrect Default Permissions vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Least Privilege Violation vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privilege and Denial of Service.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command Execution and Launch of Phishing Attacks.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution.

IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.
title: IBM Engineering AI hub Cross-Site Scripting

desc: IBM Financial Transaction Manager (FTM) 3.2.13.0 through 3.2.13.0 Interim Fix 006 stores potentially sensitive information in environment variables that could be read by a local user.
title: IBM Financial Transaction Manager v3 is vulnerable to sensitive information exposure

desc: IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration.
title: IBM Engineering AI hub Origin Validation Error

desc: Todoist MCP Server provides tools that allow AI agents to access and modify a Todoist account. Prior to 10.3.3, the optional todoist-mcp-http server accepts browser-origin requests to POST /mcp without validating the Host and Origin headers or authenticating the browser caller. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to reach the loopback listener and invoke MCP tools through StreamableHTTPServerTransport, which uses the server-held Todoist API key. This exposes Todoist account data and permits operations such as task creation, updates, completion, and deletion. The stdio transport is not browser-reachable and is not affected by this attack path. This issue is fixed in version 10.3.3.
title: Todoist MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding lets websites write and delete Todoist data through local MCP server

desc: cassandra-jdbc-wrapper provides a JDBC-compliant API over the Java driver for Apache Cassandra. Prior to 4.16.4 and 5.0.2, DriverUtil.toStringWithoutSensitiveValues() and DriverUtil.redactSensitiveValuesInJdbcUrl() redact the password property but not the equally sensitive token property used for DataStax Astra and other token-based authentication. When DEBUG logging is enabled, SessionHolder passes connection properties and JDBC URLs containing token through these helpers, causing the live token to be written in plaintext when connections are acquired or released. An attacker who can read those logs can use the token to access Cassandra data and operations authorized to that credential. This issue is fixed in versions 4.16.4 and 5.0.2.
title: cassandra-jdbc-wrapper: Authentication Token Exposed in Logs

desc: Outstatic is a static site CMS for Markdown and MDX content stored in GitHub repositories. Prior to 2.2.1, the authenticated GitHub REST proxy accepts an unvalidated endpoint value, constructs an upstream URL by string concatenation, and attaches the current dashboard user's GitHub OAuth token without ensuring the destination remains the exact GitHub API origin. An authenticated dashboard user can cause the server to send that user's token to a non-GitHub host, potentially exposing private repositories and other resources allowed by the token's scopes. The issue does not let an unauthenticated attacker access private data and does not directly expose another user's token without an additional same-origin execution or request-forging primitive. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.1.
title: Outstatic: Authenticated GitHub REST proxy can send OAuth token to non-GitHub origins

desc: Tapir is a Scala library for describing HTTP APIs and exposing, consuming, and documenting them using open standards. Prior to 1.13.27, tapir-openapi-codegen-core generates Scala source from untrusted OpenAPI documents by interpolating object property names, query, header, and path parameter names, and operation tags without context-appropriate validation or escaping. Crafted names or values can break out of generated identifier or string-literal contexts and inject arbitrary Scala that executes when generated code is compiled or endpoints are assembled. This is a code-generation and build-time issue and does not make a running tapir server directly exploitable. This issue is fixed in version 1.13.27.
title: Tapir: Construction/decode RCE via property name -> raw case-class field (tapir-openapi-codegen)

desc: LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
title: LLMKube: Arbitrary Host File Read via Model.spec.source hostPath Injection

desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to .8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5, the Security Server writes each downloaded federated global-configuration part under the X-Road instance identifier declared by the part itself without checking that the identifier matches the source ecosystem that signed and delivered it. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide a validly signed SHARED-PARAMETERS part naming a victim ecosystem, causing the part to be written as the victim's authoritative shared-params.xml. The poisoned configuration can persist across refreshes, add attacker-controlled trust material, and enable impersonation of victim members and Security Servers across every ecosystem federated with the malicious source. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5.
title: X-Road: Cross-instance global configuration poisoning via federated download

desc: mssql-mcp-core is the shared library that powers MSSQL MCP servers. Prior to core and server 0.6.0 and reader and writer 0.5.0, multiple database tools interpolate caller-controlled identifiers and predicates into T-SQL batches passed to Request.query() while parameterizing only data values. update_data, delete_data, insert_data, execute_transaction, create_table, create_index, and drop_table accept unsafe tableName, column, index, schema, or free-form whereClause input, while reader-tier list_databases interpolates stateFilter without runtime allowlist enforcement. Row-count and preview queries execute before confirmUpdate or confirmDelete, allowing malicious arguments to bypass confirmation and maxRows controls and execute stacked DDL or DML, read or destroy data, and potentially run operating-system commands when the SQL login is privileged and xp_cmdshell is enabled. This issue is fixed in core and server version 0.6.0 and reader and writer version 0.5.0.
title: mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses

desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2 and 7.7.3, the Configuration Proxy uses attacker-controlled Content-location metadata from a validly signed federated global configuration part when constructing an output path without verifying that the resulting path remains inside the intended configuration output directory. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide an absolute path or directory traversal sequence during the normal refresh cycle, causing the Configuration Proxy to create a new file with attacker-controlled content under the permissions of the non-privileged xroad process. The vulnerability can poison downstream global configuration or create files in other writable locations, but it does not overwrite existing files. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2 and 7.7.3.
title: X-Road: Arbitrary file creation via malicious global configuration in the X-Road Configuration Proxy

desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4, HashChainVerifier in the common-message module resolves attacker-controlled batch-signature hash chains before verifying the message signature and signing certificate, without cycle detection, recursion-depth or total-step limits, or per-step memoization. A registered ecosystem member can send a small crafted hashchain MIME part with repeated or cyclic StepRef values so that verifyHashChain() performs exponential work or unbounded recursion before authentication. Repeated requests can exhaust Security Server proxy threads and deny data-exchange service, and a self-reference can raise an uncaught error. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4.
title: X-Road: Pre-authentication DoS in batch hash-chain verification on the Security Server

desc: A weakness has been identified in Directus up to 12.6.1. Affected by this issue is the function getSecret of the file api/src/services/shares.ts of the component Share Login Service. This manipulation causes incorrect authorization. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
title: Directus Share Login Service shares.ts getSecret authorization

desc: A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows remote attackers to hijack the authentication of administrators and perform unauthorized state-changing actions, such as adding, editing, or deleting posts and sub-admins, or changing passwords, via crafted HTTP requests. This occurs because the application fails to implement anti-CSRF tokens for admin actions and permits destructive operations via HTTP GET requests.

A Session Fixation vulnerability exists in the admin login endpoint (/admin/index.php) of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The application fails to regenerate the session identifier (PHPSESSID) upon successful authentication. A remote attacker can exploit this by setting a known session ID in the victim's browser prior to login. Once the victim authenticates, the attacker can reuse the fixed session ID to hijack the victim's authenticated session.

The rsyslog's`imuxsock` special parser can end up writing into the received message raw buffer when trying to replace the message timestamp with the system's timestamp. A local attacker with the ability to write to the `imuxsock` socket can leverage that by crafting a malformed PRI value with a short timestamp to lead the rsyslog to perform the out-of-bounds write.
title: Rsyslog: rsyslog's imuxsock special parser can write beyond a received message's raw buffer when replacing the message timestamp

desc: An Unrestricted File Upload vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows authenticated attackers to upload files with arbitrary content by bypassing weak filename extension validation in add-post.php and change-image.php. Although files are renamed with an image extension upon storage, the lack of MIME type and content validation enables content spoofing, storage of malicious markup, and creates a vector for Remote Code Execution (RCE) with server misconfigurations or secondary Local File Inclusion.

A flaw was found in the Ansible language server shipped with the vscode-ansible extension. The regular expression used to extract documentation fragments from Ansible module files is susceptible to quadratic-time scanning. A module file containing a crafted documentation string causes the language server to consume excessive CPU while indexing it, freezing the language service in the developer's editor. An attacker who can get a developer to open or index a workspace containing an attacker-supplied collection can cause a denial of service of the editor language features. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Vscode-ansible: denial of service via quadratic documentation-regex scanning in the ansible language server

desc: A flaw was found in ansible-builder. The regular expression used to strip comments from a collection's requirements.txt during introspection is susceptible to super-quadratic backtracking. A requirements file containing a line with a long run of internal whitespace and no comment character causes the comment-stripping routine to consume CPU time proportional to the square of the line length. An attacker who can get a victim to build an execution environment that includes an attacker-supplied collection can cause the ansible-builder build or introspect process to hang, resulting in a denial of service. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Ansible-builder: denial of service via super-quadratic regular expression backtracking in ansible-builder requirements parsing

desc: install-artifact-from-github installs prebuilt native artifacts hosted by GitHub without compiling them locally. Prior to 1.7.0, bin/install-from-cache.js downloads a native .node artifact, allows RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR to select a source, follows HTTP redirects including HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrades, and writes the decompressed response to the artifact path without cryptographic integrity verification before writing or loading it. An attacker who controls a configured mirror, replaces a release asset, or can modify plaintext transport can supply native code that executes when the consumer loads the artifact. Version 1.7.0 adds SHA-256 verification for default-GitHub-source downloads when the consuming package publishes an artifactHashes bag; configured mirrors and packages without a bag remain outside that verification.
title: install-artifact-from-github loads downloaded native artifacts without integrity verification

desc: Miren Runtime provides the runtime component for the Miren application platform. Prior to 0.11.1, the QUIC/HTTP3 RPC server on the default port 8443 uses tls.RequestClientCert and does not verify that presented certificates chain to the configured cluster certificate authority. The RPC authenticators derive a caller identity from PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName without requiring a non-empty VerifiedChains value, and certificate identities bypass all RBAC checks. A network attacker who can reach the listener can present a self-signed certificate with an issuer distinguished name matching the public cluster CA subject and gain cluster superuser access, allowing disclosure, modification, or disruption of applications, sandboxes, disks, credentials, and other managed resources. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.
title: Miren Runtime: Authentication bypass in RPC layer: unverified TLS client certificates grant cluster superuser access

desc: cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services. Prior to 1.1.2, worker/src/routes/workers.ts uses bare fetch(url) calls to retrieve user-supplied URLs and deploys the returned content as a Worker script using stored Cloudflare credentials. The multipart and JSON branches of POST /api/:accountId/workers and POST /api/batch-deploy accept URLs without protocol, destination, redirect, content-type, or response-size validation. An attacker with deployment API access, or unauthenticated access when API_SECRET is not configured, can make cf-manager access internal resources or fetch attacker-controlled JavaScript and execute it in the victim Cloudflare Workers account. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.2.
title: cf-manager: SSRF via URL-based Worker deployment allows arbitrary code execution in victim Cloudflare accounts

desc: The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.
title: Datadog Agent: Datadog SSI Injector Contains Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

desc: ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.
title: ALTCHA PHP: verifySolution bypasses HMAC signature check when challenge signature is absent

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/user_manager.ajax.php exposes the update_users action without an authorization check and stores attacker-controlled firstname, lastname, and email values without HTML sanitization. An unauthenticated attacker can modify another user's profile fields, and the stored content executes when user_portal.php, the administrative user listing, user information, social profile, course participant list, or message-composer recipient header renders the modified account. Targeting an administrator account can expose administrator-session data or permit actions in that session. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.
title: Chamilo LMS: Stores XSS in update_users

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/record_audio_rtc.ajax.php concatenates the user-controlled audio_dir parameter with the course document root and passes the result to recursive directory creation without path normalization. An authenticated course user can select directory paths outside the intended course storage tree wherever the web-server account has permission to create directories. The resulting filesystem changes can interfere with application layout or support a separate file-write or code-execution chain, although this endpoint alone is not shown to write attacker-selected file content outside the course tree. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.
title: Chamilo LMS: Path Traversal / Arbitrary Directory Creation through audio recording feature

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/dropbox/dropbox_functions.inc.php accepts a literal .htaccess filename in the course dropbox and stores it in a directory served by Apache, where the file can alter handler behavior under the required AllowOverride All configuration. Any authenticated course participant can upload .htaccess and then upload a PHP payload disguised as a .gif, resulting in code execution as the web-server user when the dropbox tool is enabled. This can expose or modify the Chamilo installation, course content, and database credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.
title: Chamilo LMS: Authenticated RCE through .htaccess in dropbox

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, main/lp/scormItem.class.php and public/main/lp/scormItem.class.php store an attacker-controlled title element from imsmanifest.xml without cross-site scripting sanitization when a teacher imports a SCORM package. The title reaches c_lp_item.title and is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/LearnPath/scorm_list.html.twig through item.title with raw output while Twig auto-escaping is disabled; the default configuration does not apply the optional AI-disclosure sanitization path. Enrolled students or administrators who view the learning-path table of contents can execute the stored content in their browser sessions. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.
title: Chamilo LMS: Stored XSS in Learning Path TOC via malicious SCORM package item title

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, POST /api/social_posts accepts attacker-controlled content that SocialPost::setContent stores without cross-site scripting sanitization, and assets/vue/components/social/SocialWallPost.vue renders post.content through v-html without sanitization. Any authenticated user can create a social-wall post that executes active content when another authenticated user views the wall. The script can run in an administrator's browser session and expose session data or perform actions with the victim's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.
title: Chamilo LMS: Stored XSS in Social Wall post content via API (v-html without DOMPurify)

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the BigBlueButton plugin is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) injection when an authenticated administrator configures a malicious BigBlueButton server URL. Processing attacker-controlled XML from that server can read arbitrary local files and perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Sensitive configuration, credentials, source code, and internal network resources may be exposed. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.
title: Chamilo LMS: XXE Injection Vulnerability in BigBlueButton Plugin

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, src/Chamilo/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php and src/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php use paths supplied by an imported legacy course backup without consistently confining them to the extraction directory. A course teacher can import a crafted backup containing parent-directory path segments, causing file operations to write attacker-controlled content outside the intended destination, including PHP-executable or automatically loaded locations. This can result in code execution as the PHP process and compromise course data, user data, credentials, and the host. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.
title: Chamilo LMS: ZIP Slip / Path Traversal in CourseRestorer leads to arbitrary file write and RCE by any course teacher

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line and in 2.0.0, plugin/cleandeletedfiles/src/ajax.php and public/plugin/CleanDeletedFiles/src/ajax.php pass the request path parameter and list parameter directly to unlink without canonicalization, filename validation, or confinement to the plugin's scanned directories. An authenticated administrator can delete arbitrary files writable by the web server; a cross-site request forgery against an administrator session can reach the same operation. Deleting application source, uploaded content, cache, or configuration files can cause data loss and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line. No fixed 2.0 release is established as of this review.
title: Chamilo LMS CleanDeletedFiles plugin permits arbitrary file deletion

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.1, main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php and public/main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php trust the request uid parameter instead of the authenticated user identity when saving SCORM learning objectives. Any authenticated student can replace uid with another user's identifier and overwrite that user's objectives because the endpoint performs no ownership check. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.1.
title: Chamilo LMS: IDOR in lp_ajax_save_objectives.php — Attacker Can Overwrite Any User's SCORM Objectives via uid Parameter

desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, public/main/course_description/course_description_controller.php assigns contentDescription directly from a teacher's request in the Doctrine-based add and edit paths without cross-site scripting sanitization. The stored value is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/Course/about.html.twig through description with raw output, and the /course/{id}/about route is publicly accessible. A teacher can store active content that executes when an authenticated or unauthenticated visitor views the course description, enabling session theft, credential phishing, defacement, or actions in an authenticated victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.
title: Chamilo LMS: Stored XSS in course description controller via contentDescription field

desc: Incus from 7.3.0 before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest API that allows a process in one container to impersonate another by creating a cgroup named with a forged lxc.monitor. component. Attackers can read the target container's user.* and cloud-init.* configuration and devices, subscribe to its events, mark it ready, and export images across projects.
title: Incus 7.3.0 before 7.6.0 Guest API Container Impersonation via Forged Cgroup

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows users who can launch instances from controlled images to inject LXC directives by embedding line breaks in OCI config.json values or oci.entrypoint and oci.cwd keys. Attackers can add liblxc hooks or crafted tmpfs lxc.mount.entry fields to run commands as root on the host or bind-mount host paths, even from restricted projects.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 LXC Configuration Injection via OCI Image Config

desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 7.3.0 before 7.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the smwtask API check-query task that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass object-level authorization by relying on the wiki-wide edit right. Attackers can supply arbitrary subject titles, including protected pages, to run synchronous Semantic MediaWiki queries with caller-controlled conditions, limit, offset, and querymode parameters.
title: SemanticMediaWiki 7.3.0 before 7.4.0 Missing Authorization in smwtask check-query

desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.
title: SemanticMediaWiki 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 Stored XSS via Special:Browse Allows Pattern

desc: Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in financial reporting endpoints that allows low-privilege authenticated users to generate reports outside their permitted scope. Attackers can send crafted requests to affected reporting endpoints to read other companies' tax and payment data, including personal and corporate identifiers and financial totals.
title: Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 Missing Authorization in Financial Reporting Endpoints

desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and separator parameters. Attackers can craft Special:Ask links using request_type=special_page so export output renders as text/html, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers under the wiki origin.
title: SemanticMediaWiki 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 Reflected XSS via Special:Ask CSV/DSV Separators

desc: Finsys Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users with stacks:edit permission to move arbitrary server directories by supplying a crafted oldDir parameter. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/stacks/[name]/relocate with an unvalidated source path to relocate directories into stack paths, disrupting services and exposing their contents.
title: Finsys Dockhand before 1.0.55 Path Traversal via Stack Relocate oldDir Parameter

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the storage bucket S3 listener, which buffers entire signed request bodies in memory before verifying the signature or credential role. Attackers knowing only a valid access key, or holding a read-only credential, can send many concurrent large requests to exhaust daemon memory.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Memory Exhaustion via S3 Listener Pre-Authentication Buffering

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted and view-only clients to read default project resources by requesting the default project directly. Attackers knowing resource names can read profiles, images, network zone peer keys and stored credentials, and export custom volume or bucket backups to obtain full contents or S3 admin keys.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Improper Authorization Exposes Default Project Resources

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious migration peers to write outside intended directories by supplying unvalidated dependent volume and snapshot names in the migration offer header. Attackers controlling a migration source can create root-owned volumes with attacker content at arbitrary host paths, compromising hosts using dir storage pools, bypassing restricted.storage-pools.access, or crashing the daemon.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Path Traversal via Dependent Volumes in Migration

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 exposes certificate and cluster join token secrets through the default project event stream and skips authorization when cancelling operations without associated permissions. Restricted clients can subscribe to operation events to capture certificate tokens and enroll unrestricted certificates, gaining full server access, or cancel token operations by UUID.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Token Exposure and Missing Authorization via Operation Events

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted clients to create and access default project resources by exploiting entitlement checks against the requested project. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq directives to execute code as root on the host, or manipulate inherited resources via the ?project= parameter.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Authorization Bypass via Default Project Resource Inheritance

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project-restricted authenticated clients to receive other projects' OVN ACL logs because these events are broadcast with an empty project. Attackers can subscribe to network-acl events on one accessible project to observe internal IPs, ports, protocols, and allow/drop decisions across all projects.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Cross-Project Information Disclosure via OVN ACL Events

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to authenticate as any trusted certificate by appending its public certificate to their presented TLS client chain. Attackers can append the server's or a cluster member's certificate to gain cluster-level access, bypass authorization, modify trust store entries, and influence scriptlet-based authorization decisions.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Authentication Bypass via Unverified Client Certificate Chains

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users permitted to import custom volumes to store unvalidated snapshot names from the backup index configuration section. Attackers can craft a backup with traversal sequences in snapshot names so later deletion removes arbitrary host directories as root, while renaming or mounting operates on arbitrary paths.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Path Traversal via Custom Volume Backup Snapshot Names

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability: rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container makes it boot without a user namespace. Root processes inside the container run as host uid 0, keeping capabilities like sys_module, with no device cgroup restriction, letting them load kernel modules and compromise the host.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Privilege Escalation via Rebuild of Never-Started Container

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest-API image export handler that fails to pin the project parameter to the guest's own project. Container root users with the guest-API image entitlement can supply another project in the project query parameter to export public or cached images, including non-public images pulled from authenticated remotes.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Cross-Project Image Disclosure via /dev/incus Image Export

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with project event-view access to read migration websocket secrets broadcast in operation metadata. Attackers can connect to in-flight migration control and fs websockets before the legitimate peer, hijacking the transfer to obtain instance configuration and filesystem data.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Migration Hijack via Exposed Websocket Secrets

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows restricted project users to create resources in the unrestricted default project by targeting projects lacking features.* flags. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq dhcp-script injection to run scripts as root, or custom volumes with block.create_options mkfs arguments to read host files.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Project Isolation Bypass via Default Project Resource Creation

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted TLS clients to read other projects' bucket S3 keys and profile configuration through recursive and all-projects responses. Attackers can query bucket listings with recursion=2 or profiles with all-projects=true to obtain S3 secret keys and sensitive environment, cloud-init and user values across projects.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Information Disclosure via Recursive and All-Projects Responses

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 creates the NBD servers used for virtual machine migration and disk export on abstract unix sockets, which have no permission checks and whose names are visible in /proc/net/unix. A local unprivileged user can connect while an operation runs to read or modify the VM disk, gaining code execution in the guest on a migration's receiving side.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 VM Disk Hijacking via Abstract NBD Unix Sockets

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 fails to reject special files, hard links, or symlinks in backup or image metadata, allowing restricted project users to read or overwrite host files. Attackers can import crafted backups containing device nodes, a hard-linked backup.yaml, or symlinks to corrupt host storage, overwrite host files, or leak other projects' data.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Host File Read/Overwrite via Backup or Image Metadata

desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows clients permitted to create instances to crash the daemon by importing a backup with a null snapshot entry in index.yaml. Attackers can trigger an unrecovered nil pointer dereference during configuration rewrite, terminating the daemon and all containers and virtual machines on the node.
title: Incus before 7.6.0 Denial of Service via Null Snapshot Entry in Backup

desc: Obot from 0.26.0 before 0.27.0 fails to validate the resource identifier in remote MCP server protected resource metadata, allowing malicious MCP servers to steal access tokens. Attackers can name a different service and authorization server with chosen scopes, causing Obot to obtain the victim's token for that service and forward it to the attacker.
title: Obot 0.26.0 before 0.27.0 Access Token Theft via OAuth Resource Metadata

desc: Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.
title: Obot 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 Command Injection via Docker MCP Server File Setup

desc: Obot from 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power Users to bypass outbound protections by supplying unspecified addresses, IPv6 transition addresses, or registry icon URLs. Attackers can add remote MCP servers pointing to 0.0.0.0, ::, or NAT64/6to4/Teredo addresses embedding blocked IPv4 addresses to probe internal services for reachability.
title: Obot 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 SSRF Protection Bypass via MCP Server URLs

desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows enrolled hosts to trigger unbounded per-name database lookups by submitting osquery result logs. Attackers with a valid host node key can send one request to /api/osquery/log containing many distinct query names, exhausting database connections and read replica capacity.
title: Fleet before 4.92.0 Denial of Service via osquery Result Log Submission

desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated observer-level users to sort software listings by arbitrary columns via the order_key parameter. Attackers can order by joined hosts table columns such as node keys and use pagination as a binary-search oracle to extract sensitive column values.
title: Fleet before 4.92.0 SQL Injection via order_key Parameter

desc: Obot before 0.27.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass same-site validation of the rd parameter by inserting a tab character. Attackers can craft sign-in or sign-out links on the Obot domain that browsers resolve to external hosts, redirecting victims to phishing pages.
title: Obot before 0.27.0 Open Redirect via Tab Character in rd Parameter

desc: Obot from 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power User accounts to reach internal hosts by advertising a malicious OAuth token endpoint in remote MCP server metadata. Attackers can direct token exchange or refresh requests, including redirected GET requests, to cloud metadata services or private-network hosts and read error response bodies.
title: Obot 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 SSRF via OAuth Token Endpoint

desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in the host inventory export endpoint that allows attackers controlling an enrolled host or enroll secret to plant spreadsheet formulas. Attackers can set osquery-reported fields like hostname or hardware serial to formula values, enabling data exfiltration or DDE command execution when users open the exported CSV.
title: Fleet before 4.92.0 CSV Formula Injection via Host Inventory Export

desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse case-mutated security tokens because MySQL token columns used case-insensitive collation. Attackers holding a case-normalized invite or email-change token can redirect a victim's email for account takeover or redeem invites with roles up to Global Admin.
title: Fleet before 4.92.0 Case-Insensitive Security Token Comparison Account Takeover

desc: Froxlor before 2.3.16 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to read hidden traffic statistics by calling the Traffic.listing API command. Attackers can authenticate to api.php with their API key and secret to retrieve HTTP, FTP, and mail traffic volumes despite the panel.customer_hide_options restriction.
title: Froxlor before 2.3.16 Authorization Bypass via Traffic.listing API Command

desc: pnpm exe before 10.34.8 embeds an outdated Node.js runtime that still trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates during registry TLS connections. Network attackers holding a recovered intermediate key can intercept standalone pnpm registry fetches and serve forged package metadata or tarballs.
title: pnpm exe before 10.34.8 Trusts Compromised eMudhra Intermediate Certificates

desc: Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SAML SSO callback that looks up sessions using unvalidated client-supplied identifiers. Users able to run live queries or enroll secret holders can plant attacker-controlled identity provider metadata in the session store, then present a self-signed SAML response to log in as a global admin.
title: Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 SAML SSO Authentication Bypass via Session Store Keys

desc: Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via unbounded BER recursion in PKCS#7 parsing. Attackers can send deeply nested indefinite-length structures to Apple MDM check-in, enrollment, SCEP, or OTA endpoints to crash the entire Fleet instance.
title: Fleet before 4.86.2 Unauthenticated DoS via Apple MDM PKCS#7 Parsing

desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the deprecated POST /api/latest/fleet/mdm/apple/enqueue endpoint that allows team-scoped users to enqueue Apple MDM commands outside their teams. Attackers with team admin, maintainer, or GitOps roles can include one own-team host UUID alongside unresolved enrollment IDs to send commands like InstallProfile to deleted or user-channel enrollments without activity logging.
title: Fleet before 4.92.0 Authorization Bypass via Deprecated Apple MDM Enqueue Endpoint

desc: heym before 0.0.142 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Playwright step-mode node where _resolve_expressions_in_code substitutes workflow values directly into generated Python source. Authenticated non-admin users can craft step field values that break out of string literals to execute arbitrary Python as root inside the backend container.
title: heym before 0.0.142 Authenticated RCE via Playwright Step-Mode String Fields

desc: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before commit d38658bedbdd811b798da16b49301478c6cf21af grants '/*' file read in its rpcd read ACL, which rpcd's fnmatch matching applies to every path. Users delegated only luci-app-uhttpd read access can read any file as root, including /etc/shadow, /etc/config/* credentials, /etc/uhttpd.key, and /etc/dropbear keys.
title: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before d38658b Filesystem-Wide File Read via ACL

desc: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate on master before 3.0.0-1, on openwrt-25.12 before 2.4.9-6, and on openwrt-24.10 and openwrt-23.05 (no fix available) grants file exec permissions for state-mutating commands in the read scope of its rpcd ACL, letting authenticated read-only users run those commands as root. Attackers can invoke ubus file exec on /etc/init.d/travelmate setup, start, stop, restart, or /sbin/ifup to modify and commit network and firewall configuration or disrupt the travelmate daemon.
title: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate before 3.0.0-1 and 2.4.9-6 Improper Access Control via Read ACL

desc: Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind interface. Attackers controlling a localhost-origin page or DNS-rebinding name can read unauthenticated /tools and /health responses, exposing tool catalogs and bridge metadata on non-loopback binds.
title: Network-AI 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 CORS Misconfiguration via McpStreamableServer

desc: All versions of LaraDashboard contain an authentication bypass in SocialAuthService::findOrCreateUser(), which links a social login to an existing account by email without checking that the OAuth provider verified that email. Unauthenticated attackers using an OAuth/OIDC provider that asserts a victim's email can log in as any user, including Superadmin, and keep persistent access through a linked social_accounts entry.
title: LaraDashboard Account Takeover via Unverified OAuth Email in SocialAuthService

desc:
Relative path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon Multimodal before 1.6.0 might allow adversary-in-the-middle attackers to write arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running the tool via a crafted dataset archive substituted for a dataset downloaded over plaintext HTTP.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade autogluon.multimodal to version 1.6.0 or later.
title: Path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon Multimodal

desc: An insecure password reset vulnerability in the Admin Password Recovery Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to change an administrator or sub-administrator account password by providing the corresponding username and email address. The application does not require verification of account ownership through an email token, OTP, or another authentication mechanism before updating the password, potentially resulting in account takeover.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Public News Article Rendering Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows authenticated attackers with administrative or sub-administrative privileges to inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript through the postdescription parameter when creating or editing news articles. The application renders the stored post content without proper output encoding in news-details.php, allowing injected JavaScript to execute in the browsers of users who visit the affected article.

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The $currenturl variable in news-details.php is constructed using unencoded REQUEST_URI and HTTP_HOST server variables and echoed directly into the href attributes of social share links. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL containing HTML metacharacters to break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the context of the victim's browser.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System v2.1 contains an insufficient verification vulnerability in the password recovery functionality in forgot-password.php. The application allows an unauthenticated user to access the password-change workflow by providing a valid employee ID and corresponding email address without requiring an additional out-of-band verification mechanism.
PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V 1.1 is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in admin/search-invoices.php via the searchdata parameter.

PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V1.1 uses a non-cryptographic function to generate security-sensitive appointment and invoice identifiers. The identifiers are generated within a restricted numeric range and are subsequently used in record lookup operations. This implementation exposes the application to identifier prediction or guessing attacks under conditions where the identifiers are relied upon as a security boundary.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System V2.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because database backup files are stored within the publicly accessible web root. An unauthenticated remote attacker can download the SQL backup files and retrieve sensitive database contents, including employee personally identifiable information and password hashes.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task or its parameters are marked no_log: true, sensitive values passed to a module's warn() or deprecate() calls are not redacted and are printed in cleartext to stdout/stderr in warning and deprecation messages. The 'warnings' and 'deprecations' keys are retained in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py when the task result is censored, so sensitive parameters bypass masking and can be disclosed in output captured in terminal sessions, CI logs, and any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true.

A flaw was found in hypershift-addon. Due to an overly permissive role-based access control (RBAC) configuration that grants permissions to all authenticated users rather than restricting them to the addon service, a low-privileged authenticated user can view, modify, or delete managed cluster resources. This improper authorization allows unauthorized users to alter or disrupt clusters across the entire managed fleet.
title: Hypershift-addon: hypershift-addon: overly permissive clusterrolebinding allows any authenticated user to modify and delete managed clusters

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to check whether the calling session originated from an OAuth authorization grant, which allows a third-party application holding a delegated access token to register a new, independent OAuth application under the identity of the delegating user via the OAuth application registration endpoint.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00780
title: Missing authorization check in Mattermost OAuth application registration

desc: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to bound the work performed while reading EXIF orientation metadata, which allows an authenticated user to cause disproportionate server-side CPU usage by uploading or linking a small image with specially structured EXIF metadata.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00784
title: Uncontrolled CPU consumption via EXIF metadata in image orientation handling

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the Access Control Policy's download_file_attachment check across several post- and file-serving code paths (bulk post retrieval, channel bookmarks, and persistent notification delivery), which allows an authenticated channel member denied a specific file's download to obtain that file's metadata and a rendered preview thumbnail via those endpoints and events.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00785
title: Missing authorization check in Mattermost Server exposes restricted file metadata across multiple delivery paths

desc: A vulnerability in the Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxScanTime and cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV OLE2 parser to get into an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the eXtensible ARchive (XAR) GZIP file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxFileSize and cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the XAR GZIP file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted XAR GZIP file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV to exceed the MaxFileSize and potentially get caught in an infinite loop, causing a DoS condition.

A vulnerability in the InstallShield file parser of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to incomplete error checking when the InstallShield File Parser is performing a scan. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted InstallShield file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to logic error when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to allocate all available memory, causing the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the LZX data algorithm for Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning in ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper boundary checks when applying the LZX data algorithm to CHM files during the decoder stage, which may result in buffer overflow. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the debug logging functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper handling of logging values. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a file to be scanned by the software that has debug logging enabled. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Ultimate Packer for eXecutables (UPX) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to improper length checks, when unpacking the UPX files, which may result in an out-of-bounds read of heap memory. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted UPX for decode. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems. From 5.4.8 until 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1, mint-refresh-cache passes a user-controlled --parent-window-id value directly to the privileged Synaptic process without validating it as an integer. A local user permitted to execute mint-refresh-cache through sudo can inject additional Synaptic command-line options and achieve arbitrary code execution as root. This issue is fixed in versions 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1.
title: Linux Mint Update Manager: Local Privilege Escalation in mint-refresh-cache

desc:
A vulnerability in the phishcheck functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper allocation of memory during processing of URLs. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a URL to be processed by the software. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to a logic error when scanning the CHM file and following the internal file pointers. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Yoda'a Crytper (yC) Portable Executable (PE) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. .
 This vulnerability is due to lack of proper error checking for negative values when processing the PE file to be unpacked. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a PE file to be unpacked. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce playbook membership management permissions when creating a new playbook which allows a low-privileged user to grant the playbook_admin role to an arbitrary user via a crafted playbook creation request. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00749
title: Missing authorization check on playbook creation allows unauthorized assignment of the playbook_admin role in Mattermost Playbooks

desc: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce the configured GitLab group/namespace restriction on the permalink code-preview feature and the {{get_projects}} MCP tool, which allows an authenticated user with a connected GitLab account to retrieve repository file content or project metadata from projects outside the restricted group via a crafted GitLab permalink or MCP tool call. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00750
title: Improper Namespace Access Restriction in Mattermost GitLab Plugin (Permalink Preview and MCP get_projects)

desc: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to scope an incoming webhook's direct message target to the webhook's own team, which allows a team administrator to deliver a direct message to a user on a team they have no authority over via a webhook whose posting identity belongs to both teams.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00751
title: Mattermost incoming webhooks allow cross-team direct messages under team restriction

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to sanitize terminal escape sequences when rendering server logs via {{mmctl logs}}, which allows an unauthenticated attacker to hijack a system administrator's clipboard or spoof terminal output via a crafted HTTP request whose logged content is later viewed with {{mmctl logs}}. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00753
title: Incomplete Fix for Terminal Escape Sequence Injection in {{mmctl logs}}

desc: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to enforce the team view permission across all filter combinations of the user listing endpoint which allows an authenticated user to enumerate the membership of a team they are not permitted to view via a crafted request to that endpoint.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00755
title: Improper access control in Mattermost user listing API exposes team membership

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 Fail to revoke a user's active sessions when a bulk import links an existing user account to a bot record or changes the account's auth_service/auth_data, which allows an attacker in possession of a session token issued before the import to retain full authenticated access to the affected account via a system administrator-triggered bulk import job.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00746
title: Sessions not revoked on account conversion or auth rebinding via bulk import

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to invalidate cached WebSocket session state when an OAuth app is deleted, which allows a revoked OAuth integration to keep receiving real-time events, including private channel posts, via a WebSocket connection that was already open when the app was deleted.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00745
title: Revoked OAuth app retains access to real-time events via already-open WebSocket connection

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to bound the resources consumed while processing an uploaded custom emoji image which allows an authenticated user with default permissions to make the server unresponsive for all users via repeated custom emoji uploads.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00720
title: Uncontrolled resource consumption in Mattermost custom emoji upload allows server disruption

desc: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to sanitize channel mentions when rendering permalinked posts, which allows an authenticated user to discover the display names of private channels they do not have access to via a permalink to a post that mentions the channel.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00721
title: Private channel name disclosure via unsanitized channel mentions in Mattermost permalinked posts

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the channel Access Control Policy's file download permission check when serving file metadata and thumbnails through the drafts, scheduled posts, and post edit history endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has lost eligibility under the policy to view metadata and thumbnails of file attachments via those endpoints, even though direct file access is correctly denied. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00740
title: Access Control Policy Bypass via Drafts, Scheduled Posts, and Post Edit History Exposes Restricted File Attachments

desc:
Mattermost versions 11.8.x <= 11.8.5, 11.7.x <= 11.7.10, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fails to validate the type of card property fields which allows a board
Editor to make a board or card permanently unopenable for all users via a crafted PATCH
request storing a non-string property name or value.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00743
title: Missing type validation on card property fields in Boards allows persistent denial of service

desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the MFA requirement on the update and delete user endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has not configured MFA to modify or delete their own account via the API despite system-wide MFA enforcement being enabled. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00744
title: MFA enforcement bypass on user profile update and delete endpoints

desc: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 privilege escalation was possible via Basic authentication with a restricted access token
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 privilege escalation was possible by issuing new tokens from a restricted access token
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Promote build dialog was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Docker Container Info tab was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Disk Usage and Build Time pages was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 DoS via agent command results was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 privilege escalation to system administrator was possible after disabling per-project permissions
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 improper authorization allowed viewing build process details via agent stacktraces
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 improper authorization allowed project viewers to change project IDs
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Shared Resources build feature was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in project import archives
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in the pipeline YAML file path
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in the external artifact cache

In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 missing authorization in the Kubernetes integration allowed project viewers to use stored credentials
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 XXE via Maven settings file upload was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 XXE in the .NET build steps auto-discovery was possible

Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability. Exploiting this vulnerability allows a user to view the names of other users/companies on the platform by iterating over the numerical value that identifies the customer in  'ClientesEventos' parameter in'/Clientes/ClientesEventos/'.
title: Vulnerability in winCRM

desc: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability. Exploiting this vulnerability allows a user to view the names of other users/companies on the platform by iterating over the numerical value that identifies the customer in  'DocumentosOpcionesImprimir' parameter in'/Gestion/DocumentosOpcionesImprimir/'.
title: Vulnerability in winCRM
